note: Warm up first and move with control. Choose a weight you can move with good form for every rep. Stop if you feel pain, dizziness or breathlessness. If you are pregnant, recovering from surgery or have a heart, blood-pressure or other medical condition, check with your doctor first.

how: Feet a little wider than the hips, kettlebell in front.
Hinge at the hips, hike the bell back between the legs.
Drive the hips forward to float the bell to chest height; let it fall back into the hinge.
The power comes from the hips, not the arms.
items.caution: Keep the back flat; stop if the lower back hurts.

how: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at the chest.
Sit down between the heels, chest up, knees tracking over the toes.
Stand by pushing the floor away.
items.caution: Go only as deep as you can with a flat back.

how: Stand with the bell between the feet.
Hinge, grip the handle with straight arms, back flat.
Stand tall by driving the hips forward; lower with control.
items.caution: Keep the bell close to the body.

how: Stand or sit tall with the dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press up until the arms are straight, without arching the back.
Lower slowly to the shoulders.
items.caution: Brace the belly; reduce the weight if the back arches.

how: Hinge forward with a flat back, one hand on a bench or knee.
Pull the dumbbell toward the hip, elbow close to the body.
Lower slowly; complete all reps, then switch arms.
Stand tall with dumbbells by the sides, palms forward.
Curl up without swinging, elbows at the sides.
Lower slowly to full arm length.
Hold dumbbells by the sides and step forward.
Lower until both knees are bent about 90 degrees, back knee near the floor.
Push back to standing; alternate legs.
items.caution: Keep the front knee over the ankle.

how: Kneel on a mat and hold the wheel under the shoulders.
Brace the belly and tuck the hips slightly.
Roll forward slowly, as far as you can keep the back flat.
Pull back with the abdominals, not the arms.
items.caution: Stop short before the lower back sags; avoid with a back injury.

how: Stand with feet hip-width apart and the wheel on the floor in front.
Fold down to the wheel and roll out until the body is long and straight.
Roll back to the fold using the core; keep the hips from dropping.
Master kneeling rollouts first.
items.caution: Only when kneeling rollouts are easy; stop if the lower back aches.

how: Kneel and hold the wheel slightly to the right.
Roll forward and out at an angle to the right, keeping the hips square.
Return, then roll to the left. Each side is one rep.
items.caution: Keep the range short until you are strong at the side.

how: Kneel or come to a full plank with the hands on the wheel under the shoulders.
Hold the wheel still, belly tight, back flat, breathing steadily.
items.caution: Lower to the knees if the back sags.

how: Set the saddle so the knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the stroke; handlebar at saddle height or a little higher.
Warm up for 3 minutes with light resistance.
Work: turn the resistance knob up until it feels hard, and pedal strongly for the work time.
Rest: turn the resistance down and pedal easily until the next interval.
The heavy 10 kg flywheel keeps spinning: always slow it with the brake or resistance knob, never by stopping your legs suddenly.
Cool down with 3 minutes of easy pedalling.
items.caution: Build up gradually; stop if you feel chest pain or faintness.

items.name_en: Spin Bike Steady Ride (10 kg flywheel)
how: Set a moderate resistance and ride at a pace where you can still talk in short sentences.
Keep a smooth, steady cadence (about 70-90 turns a minute) and relaxed shoulders.
Use the resistance knob or brake to slow the flywheel at the end.
items.caution: Stop if you feel chest pain, faintness or sharp knee pain.
